abstract: BACKGROUND: Echinococcosis of the liver is a parasitic infection that poses a significant healthcare challenge in endemic regions. The majority of cases present with either no clinical signs or non-specific ones, making differential diagnosis difficult until after the operation. Preoperative diagnostics rely mainly on computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and ultrasound. The usual treatment for liver echinococcosis involves an operation, such as percutaneous intervention, surgical resection of the cyst as well as surrounding liver tissue, or major liver resection, followed by prolonged conservative treatment with Albendazole. Even though cases of simultaneous treatment of the echinococcosis and neoplastic lesions are present in the literature, they are scarce and the new data on the subject is of importance. A 61-year-old female patient presented to our clinic with chief complaint of abdominal pain. Upon physical examination, a palpable mass was discovered in the right ileac region along with hepatomegaly. Laboratory studies indicated the presence of an unspecified infection. An MRI of the abdomen revealed masses in both ovaries and cystic lesions in the liver and pelvis. The patient underwent surgical resection of cysts located both in the abdominal cavity and liver, as well as resection of surrounding liver parenchyma in S2 through S7 for echinococcosis and both-sided ovariectomy, hysterectomy, and omentum resection for lesions of the ovaries. The hepatic and abdominal cystic lesions were found to be of echinococcal origin, and the right ovary lesion was a mature teratoma even though preoperatively it was considered to be cancer. The patient is currently alive and well with no signs of recurrence after seven years. CONCLUSION: As such cases are rare, the medical documentation should be well described and analyzed for future reference. It is now considered to be possible to treat multiple cystic echinococcosis of the liver and free abdominal cavity along with potentially malignant lesions of the abdomen and pelvis - in our opinion survival rates should be similar to the rates of malignancy alone as radical surgical treatment of cystic echinococcosis remains effective and well accepted route of treatment. This rare case demonstrates and emphasizes an importance of simultaneous surgical interventions as well as correct preoperative suggestion of diagnosis.
abstract_ja: 背景: 肝包虫症は、流行地域で重大な医療上の課題となる寄生虫感染症である。大多数の症例は、臨床症状がないか、非特異的な症状を呈するため、手術後まで鑑別診断が困難である。術前の診断は主に、コンピュータ断層撮影(CT)、磁気共鳴画像法(MRI)、超音波検査に依存している。肝包虫症の治療は、経皮的治療、嚢胞および周囲の肝実質の外科的切除、または大量肝切除などの手術を伴い、その後にアルベンダゾールによる長期の保存的治療を行う。包虫症と腫瘍性病変の同時治療の症例は文献に存在するものの、その数は少なく、本テーマに関する新しいデータは重要である。症例提示: 61歳女性が腹痛を主訴に受診した。身体診察で右腸骨窩に触知可能な腫瘤と肝腫大が認められた。検査では非特異的な感染の存在が示唆された。腹部MRIで両側卵巣の腫瘤と、肝臓および骨盤内の嚢胞性病変が認められた。患者は、包虫症に対する腹腔内および肝内嚢胞の切除と、S2からS7の周囲肝実質の外科的切除、ならびに卵巣病変に対する両側卵巣摘出術、子宮摘出術、大網切除を受けた。肝臓および腹腔内の嚢胞性病変は包虫由来と判明した。右卵巣病変は成熟奇形腫であり、術前には癌と考えられていた。患者は現在、7年後も生存し、再発の徴候はない。結論: このような症例はまれであるため、将来の参照のために医療記録を十分に記載し分析すべきである。多発性の肝・腹腔内嚢胞性包虫症と、腹腔・骨盤内の潜在的に悪性の病変を同時に治療することは実行可能と考えられる。包虫症の根治的外科治療は依然として有効で広く受け入れられた治療法であるため、このような同時治療の生存率は、悪性腫瘍単独の場合と同程度になると考えられる。本稀少症例は、同時手術と正確な術前診断の重要性を示している。
